title: The Second Fastest Drive Through the Traffic Lights

concept.title: Keep two different distances per node, then replay the lights on the second one
body: Every node of a road network is a crossing with a traffic light. All the lights are green at time 0 and switch (green to red, red to green) every `change` minutes; driving along any road takes `time` minutes. You may enter a crossing at any time, but you can only **leave** it while its light is green; if it is red you wait until it turns green, and you may **not wait while it is green**. What is the second smallest *different* travel time from node 1 to node `n`? (A walk may pass the same crossing again.)

The light makes the time depend on the number of roads only: after `k` roads a drive that started at 0 is at the time `f(k)`, found by repeating "if the light is red wait for green, then add `time`". Since `f` grows with `k`, the second smallest travel time belongs to the **second smallest number of roads** of a walk from 1 to `n` (a different number from the smallest one). So the task is to find the shortest **and** the second shortest length in edges.

Every node enters the queue at most twice (once for each of its two best lengths), so the BFS takes O(n + m). The second length is always the first plus 1 or plus 2: plus 1 if some odd cycle makes it possible, otherwise plus 2 (go one road further and come back). The final loop replays the lights for the `d2[n]` roads of the answer.

statement: A connected road network has `n` crossings and `m` roads. Each crossing has a traffic light that is green at time 0 and changes colour every `change` minutes (green during [0, change), red during [change, 2 * change), and so on). Driving along a road takes `time` minutes. You leave node 1 at time 0. At a crossing you can leave only when the light is green; if it is red you wait until it is green, but you cannot wait while it is green. A walk may visit nodes (and use roads) more than once. Print the second smallest travel time from node 1 to node `n`, that is, the smallest travel time that is strictly larger than the smallest one.
inputFormat: Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: a road between the nodes `u` and `v`.
outputFormat: Print the second smallest travel time.
constraints: The graph is connected, with no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: The fastest drive 1-4-5 takes 6 minutes. The second fastest is 1-3-4-5: it reaches the node 4 at the time 6, when the light is red, waits until 10 and arrives at 13.
The drive 1-2 takes 3 minutes. The second fastest is 1-2-1-2: it is at the node 2 at the time 3 (red, wait until 4), at the node 1 at the time 7 (red, wait until 8), and at the node 2 at the time 11.

hints: The travel time depends only on the number of roads: replay the lights for that many roads.
Find the smallest and the second smallest different number of roads from 1 to n with a BFS that keeps two distances per node.
Every node is queued at most twice.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m, time, change = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

# Your code here

explanation: A BFS keeps the smallest and the second smallest different number of roads from node 1 to every node (each node enters the queue at most twice). The lights are then replayed for the second smallest number of roads of the last node: whenever the light is red the clock waits for the next green, and then the road time is added.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m + d), where d is the number of roads of the answer (at most n + 1); space O(n + m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m, time, change = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

from collections import deque
adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for u, v in edges:
    adj[u].append(v)
    adj[v].append(u)
INF = 10 ** 9
d1 = [INF] * (n + 1)
d2 = [INF] * (n + 1)
d1[1] = 0
queue = deque([(1, 0)])
while queue:
    v, d = queue.popleft()
    for w in adj[v]:
        nd = d + 1
        if nd < d1[w]:
            d1[w] = nd
            queue.append((w, nd))
        elif d1[w] < nd < d2[w]:
            d2[w] = nd
            queue.append((w, nd))
clock = 0
for _ in range(d2[n]):
    if (clock // change) % 2 == 1:
        clock = (clock // change + 1) * change
    clock += time
print(clock)
